identity.title: A Detailed View of the Circumstellar Environment and Disk of the Forming O-star AFGL 4176

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present a detailed analysis of the disk and circumstellar environment of the forming O-type star AFGL 4176 mm1, placing results from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) into context with multiwavelength data.

question.value: What are the continuum source population, spectral/morphological line properties, and large-scale environment of the disk around the forming O-star AFGL 4176 mm1, using ALMA with ATCA and APEX data?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we present a detailed analysis of the circumstellar environment and disk of AFGL 4176, combining continuum and line data from ALMA with complementary ATCA and APEX observations at 1.2-1.5 cm and 1.2 mm, respectively.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00469.S.
We also detect H29$\alpha$ with ALMA.
The angular resolutions for each spw range from 0.26 to 0.30$\ensuremath{''}$, corresponding to 1100 to 1300 au.
the total time on-source across the observations was 1.37 hr

evidence.quote: The ALMA observations of AFGL 4176 were taken in August 2014 as a Cycle 1 Transfer project during ALMA Cycle 2.

analysis_steps.goal: Identify continuum sources and measure fluxes

method.value: astrodendro on non-PB-corrected image with 5 sigma peak threshold; properties extracted from PB-corrected image

evidence.quote: we used the non-primary-beam-corrected image and set the peak flux required for a detection to be 5$\sigma$

key_parameters.value: 2 sigma flux limit; 1 sigma required difference between embedded structures

evidence.quote: the required flux difference between embedded structures to be assigned as a separate source is 1$\sigma$

validation.value: Compared with Gaussian-fit fluxes of J15

evidence.quote: The peak and integrated flux densities measured for mm1 are slightly larger than that quoted in J15, which was determined using a Gaussian fit.

method.value: Optically thin dust formulae with T=100 K (190 K for mm1)

evidence.quote: We assume a gas-to-dust ratio measured for the solar neighborhood of 154 (cite: draine11) and a temperature of 100 K, except for mm1, where we use a temperature of 190 K

assumptions.value: kappa(1.21 mm)=0.24 cm2/g; g=154; d=4.2 kpc; OH94 opacity would lower masses by ~4

evidence.quote: which if used instead would reduce the masses and column densities by a factor of $\sim$4

analysis_steps.goal: Measure mm1 spectral index and dust fraction

method.value: Power-law fit to line-free channel fluxes in 1'' aperture across spw1 and spw2; cross-check with clean nterms=2; dust fraction from f=(alpha_obs-alpha_ff)/(alpha_d-alpha_ff)

evidence.quote: We then found the integrated flux in each line-free channel within a 1$''$  diameter aperture around the mm1 peak, and subsequently fitted these continuum channel fluxes by a power law

key_parameters.value: alpha_d upper limit 3.6, alpha_ff upper limit 2

evidence.quote: Assuming an upper limit for the spectral index of dust emission of 3.6 (derived from the dust model used in J15)

fitting.value: Power-law fit; uncertainty from scatter plus calibrator-based systematic

evidence.quote: The resulting spectral index is 3.36$\pm$0.14, where the uncertainty is determined from the scatter in the data.
obtained a similar average spectral index of 3.35 over pixels within 0.15$''$ of the continuum peak

method.value: Mean spectra in 0.5'' radius aperture; >5 sigma lines; LTE models in CASSIS with CDMS/JPL; simultaneous Gaussian fits with astropy.modeling SLSQP

evidence.quote: all line properties were determined via a simultaneous spectral fit with Gaussians to all of the detected lines using `astropy.modeling` with the Sequential Least Squares Programming (SLSQP) fitter

key_parameters.value: CH3OH LTE reference: N_H2=4e25 cm-2, vLSR=-52, FWHM 5 km/s, T=160 K, size 0.5'', abundance 1e-8

fitting.value: SLSQP bounded Gaussians; errors estimated by Monte Carlo on synthetic data

evidence.quote: the errors were instead estimated by testing the fitting algorithm used with Monte Carlo simulations of synthetic data

validation.value: Compared with Bøgelund et al. 2019 line list

evidence.quote: The line identifications are generally in good agreement with (cite: bogelund19a)

method.value: Inspect channel maps; pairwise reduced chi2 on three channels (-2, 0, +2 km/s) in 2''x2'' field after adding noise to S/N 15

evidence.quote: we added noise to each of the three channels, so that all channels had a peak signal-to-noise of 15

validation.value: Self-comparison chi2 close to 1, cross-type chi2 higher

evidence.quote: the average reduced $\chi^2$ is statistically significantly higher when the $\chi^2$ is calculated from comparison between line types

method.value: Per-pixel Gaussian fits to NH3(1,1) and (2,2), Trot then Tk with Maret correction; mass from Rosolowsky eqs; ATLASGAL dust mass comparison

evidence.quote: We fit Gaussians to the main component, and hyperfine components in the case of NH$_3$(1,1), for each pixel in the NH$_3$(1,1) and NH$_3$(2,2) cubes

key_parameters.value: >7 sigma pixels, tau held at zero, NH3 abundance 10^-7.5

evidence.quote: Only pixels where the peak flux density in the main line was $>7\sigma$ in both transitions were fit.
assuming therefore that the NH$_{3}$ clump is optically thin

findings_qualitative.value: All N-bearing molecules bright enough trace the disk; O-bearing lines are mostly blue-dominant, coincident with methanol masers

evidence.quote: the presence of nitrogen in the molecules of these observations appears to indicate that it is a good disk tracer.

claims.hypothesis: mm1 continuum at 1.2 mm is dominated by dust
claims.experiment: Spectral index across ALMA band and combination with 1.23 cm flux

evidence.quote: we have determined it only contributes $<$13% and thus the majority of the emission arises from dust.

claims.hypothesis: Different molecules trace different parts of the disk environment
claims.experiment: Channel maps and chi2 comparison of lines
claims.result: Four morphology types; N-bearing disk-tracing, O-bearing blue-dominant
claims.finding: Chemical segregation; blue-dominant lines may trace accretion shock

evidence.quote: Lines that show strong emission on the blueshifted side of the disk are predominantly oxygen-bearing, which we suggest are tracing a disk accretion shock.

claims.hypothesis: mm2 is a companion or jet knot
claims.result: Rich in S-bearing lines, blueshifted, on disk axis
claims.finding: Likely a jet/outflow knot but companion not excluded

evidence.quote: although we cannot rule out that mm2 is another protostar

claims.hypothesis: mm1 lies in a large-scale rotating toroid
claims.result: Velocity gradient over r~0.5 pc, mass 9200 Msun
claims.finding: mm1 at blueshifted NW end of a rotating toroid

evidence.quote: The ATCA NH$_3$(1,1) and (2,2) emission traces a large-scale (r$\sim$0.5 pc) rotating toroid

why_this_method.value: Spectral index method chosen because Gaussian-fit continuum misses diffuse background; astrodendro used

evidence.quote: the Gaussian source lies on a background of more diffuse emission, which was not included in the Gaussian fit

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: OH94 dust opacity not used because no scattering properties for HYPERION

evidence.quote: We could not use this opacity for the radiative-transfer dust-continuum modeling presented in J15

limitations_admitted.value: Free-free contribution at 1.2 mm not removed; relative astrometry insufficient

evidence.quote: we do not attempt to remove the free-free contribution from the ALMA continuum data
